summary: Round 1, tests, on the new gate scripts/check-io-seam.sh + scripts/io_seam_scan.py and its nine-case suite buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/IoSeamGateTest.java. Everything below was MEASURED in a throwaway git worktree (scratchpad, never the live tree), each mutation applied to the gate, the suite re-run (./gradlew -p buildSrc test --tests binjava.IoSeamGateTest) and the JUnit XML parsed for which cases died; the gate was restored between runs. Baseline: 9/9 green. FOUR OF THE AUTHOR'S FIVE CLAIMED MUTATIONS REPRODUCE EXACTLY: drop the binstore-backends exemption -> kills the adapter case + the real-tree case (2/9); add bare `Clock` to BANNED -> kills the seam-parameter case + the real tree (2/9); add `java.io.` -> kills the bytes case + the real tree (2/9); skip the comment/string stripping -> kills the quoting case and ONLY that one (1/9). THE FIFTH IS OVERSTATED: widening the exemption to every module kills FIVE of nine, not all nine -- the four cases that assert exit 0 (clock seam, quoting, empty change, scope note) cannot die to a widening, by construction. The suite's strong parts are real and I verified them rather than assumed them: the real-tree count assertion is what kills the two 'read nothing' mutations, it is computed at runtime so it cannot go stale, and the javadoc's arithmetic checks out -- 103 tracked src/main binjava files, the sharp rule matches exactly one, LocalFsBinStore, in the exempt module, leaving 101 scanned, which is the number the gate prints. Each of BLOCK, LINE and STRING is individually pinned (dropping any one reds the quoting case). The wiring is pinned at the right rung and I confirmed it: deleting the hook from .pre-commit-config.yaml reds scripts/build-index.sh --check, so no test is needed for it. WHAT SURVIVES IS ONE SHAPE, THREE TIMES: the suite pins the gate by EXAMPLE, one example per family, and everything in a family that is not the example is unconstrained. Thirteen of the sixteen banned constructs can be deleted with 9/9 green. The stripping is pinned only for SINGLE-LINE comments and only for the ordering that happens not to matter. And I found a live false GREEN -- a business-logic file calling Files.readString(Path.of("/etc/hostname")) that this gate reports clean -- reachable with one char literal on the line, which is the exact defect class this repository's own review lens names ('a parser blinded by one char literal'). Five further mutations survive 9/9 on the diagnostic and error paths. The two major findings are each closable by one parameterised case; I am not asking for the production fix, only for a case that would fail without it. Tree left as found: `git diff --cached | sha256sum` is still 7b7bc9401e5f6604dfe51984de662cd6956d1a035c217cc3b2dd6fae5c0ef4c4, `git status --short` unchanged, all measurement in a detached worktree under the session scratchpad, deleted after.

findings.title: Thirteen of the sixteen banned constructs are unpinned -- deleting them from BANNED leaves 9/9 green
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION, RUN not reasoned: reduce io_seam_scan.py's BANNED list to the three needles a case actually exercises -- ('Instant.now(', 'new Socket(', 'Files.') -- deleting `LocalDate.now(`, `LocalDateTime.now(`, `ZonedDateTime.now(`, `OffsetDateTime.now(`, `System.currentTimeMillis(`, `System.nanoTime(`, `Clock.system`, `new ServerSocket(`, `new DatagramSocket(`, `HttpClient.new`, `new URL(`, `Paths.get(` and `Path.of(`. Measured: 9 of 9 cases green. The gate silently stops seeing the real clock via System.currentTimeMillis(), Clock.systemUTC(), every non-Instant .now() factory, two of the three socket constructors, HttpClient, new URL( and both remaining filesystem entry points, and nothing reds. This is not a hypothetical list: the backlog State cell added by this commit ENUMERATES all sixteen as what the gate bans, and this test's own class javadoc names three constructs as 'what is banned' -- `Instant.now()`, `System.currentTimeMillis()`, `Clock.systemUTC()` -- of which TWO have no case. Non-negotiable 2 forbids weakening a gate's threshold; a deny-list quietly losing 13 of 16 entries is that move, and the suite would not notice. Closing it is one parameterised case: for each entry in the list, a fixture file calling it must exit 1 -- ideally driven off the list itself so a needle added later is pinned by construction. RELATED AND CHEAP TO DECIDE WHILE THERE (measured, not raised as its own finding because it is the production reviewer's call, but NO case constrains it either): the match is a contiguous single-line substring, so `java.time.Instant::now` and `Files::readAllBytes` as method references are NOT seen (probed: a file whose only clock access is `Supplier<Instant> now = java.time.Instant::now;` scans clean), and neither is a call wrapped by a formatter as `java.time.Instant\n        .now();` (probed: clean).

findings.title: One char literal blinds the scanner and hides a real filesystem read; the CHAR pattern that would stop it is ordered so it cannot, and dropping it entirely leaves 9/9 green
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION, RUN: delete CHAR from code_only's tuple in io_seam_scan.py (`for pattern in (BLOCK, LINE, STRING):`). 9 of 9 green. It is not an equivalent mutant by accident of the tests -- it is DEAD CODE by construction: CHAR runs AFTER STRING, so it cannot protect the string scan from a quote inside a char literal, and a Java char literal is at most a handful of characters so it can never itself contain a needle six characters long. Its own comment ('the escape class keeps a trailing backslash from swallowing the closing quote') describes work it is ordered not to do. THE COST IS A LIVE FALSE GREEN, probed directly against the staged scanner: the business-logic file `package binjava.ingest; class E { String f(char c) { return c == '\"' ? \"yes\" : java.nio.file.Files.readString(java.nio.file.Path.of(\"/etc/hostname\")); } }` is reported CLEAN -- the quote inside the char literal mis-pairs the STRING regex, which then blanks from there to the next quote and swallows `Files.readString(java.nio.file.Path.of(`. That is a filesystem read from business logic, the exact thing this gate exists to refuse, and it is also the exact input the review packet's own lens names as a defect class already seen in this repository ('a parser blinded by one char literal'). The suite's only quoting case (aBannedCallQUOTEDInAJavadocOrASTRINGIsNotAViolation) has no char literal in its fixture, so the whole family is untested in BOTH directions. Ask: a case whose fixture carries a char literal containing a double quote on the same line as a banned call, asserting exit 1. The production fix is one edit -- put CHAR before STRING -- but a case that reds without it is what makes it stay fixed.

findings.title: The comment-stripping case pins only SINGLE-LINE comments -- dropping re.S from BLOCK survives all nine AND the real tree
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION, RUN: `BLOCK = re.compile(r'/\\*.*?\\*/')` -- drop re.S, so a block comment spanning lines is no longer stripped. 9 of 9 green. The quoting case's fixture javadoc is ONE LINE (`/** Never source the clock here -- no Instant.now(), and no Files.readAllBytes. */`), and the real-tree case cannot catch it either: I re-scanned the 101 business-logic files with re.S removed and got ZERO violations, so today's tree happens to have no banned needle inside a multi-line comment. Under the mutation the gate reds on any multi-line javadoc quoting a banned call -- which is the shape of every javadoc in this repository, and precisely the false positive this case's own javadoc says 'gets weakened rather than obeyed, which is the direction non-negotiable 2 forbids'. Probed and confirmed: a class with a two-line javadoc mentioning `Instant.now()` scans clean at HEAD and is REPORTED AS A VIOLATION under the mutation. SAME FAMILY, ALSO UNPINNED (probed against the staged scanner, no mutation needed): a Java TEXT BLOCK is not handled -- `String txt = \"\"\"\\n quoting Instant.now() inside a text block\\n\"\"\";` is reported as a violation TODAY, because the STRING regex cannot span lines. So the case's claim that 'comments and string literals are stripped' is pinned for one-line comments and one-line strings only. Ask: extend the quoting fixture's javadoc to more than one line -- that alone kills the re.S mutation -- and add a text block to it, or state in the case that text blocks are a known false positive.

findings.title: The real-tree count oracle walks the filesystem where the gate reads git, so an untracked src/main file reds a correct gate
findings.failure_scenario: NOT a surviving mutation -- a FALSE RED, measured: I added an untracked `ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/ZzUntracked.java` to the worktree and ran the suite. thisRepositoryPassesAndTheGateSaysHowManyFilesItRead FAILS, expecting '102 business-logic file(s)' while the gate correctly prints 101 -- the gate's scope is workspace_files (git ls-files + staged), the test's expectation is Files.walk minus /build/ and /binstore-backends/, and the two disagree on any untracked, unstaged .java under src/main/java/binjava/. That is not a corner case here: this very working tree carried exactly such a file (ingest/src/main/java/binjava/ingest/SegmentServing.java, untracked) at the start of the session in which the gate was written. The walk also does not exclude `.tmp/`, which exists in this repository today and holds a reference clone (`.tmp/automq`) -- 0 binjava paths, so the case is green by luck rather than by construction, and lib.sh's own doctrine plus check-gate-scope.sh exist because gates must not walk the filesystem for this reason. The independent oracle is the RIGHT idea and should not be replaced by restating scoped_files; adding `.filter(p -> !p.toString().contains(\"/.tmp/\"))` and either filtering to tracked files or asserting the count is non-zero and equals the git-derived count closes it.

findings.title: Three diagnostic and error paths are unconstrained; the unreadable-file one turns a failure into a silent pass
findings.failure_scenario: THREE SURVIVING MUTATIONS, each RUN, each 9/9 green. (a) io_seam_scan.py: delete `violations.append('%s: unreadable (%s)' % (path, e))` from the OSError handler, so a file the scanner cannot open is skipped silently instead of reported -- the gate then prints ok over a file it never read, which is the failure mode the real-tree case's own javadoc calls 'worse than a failure'. (b) io_seam_scan.py: report line 0 for every violation (`% (path, 0, needle, what)`) -- the two cases that inspect output assert only `contains(\"Dirty.java\")` and `contains(\"Instant.now(\")`, never a line number, so the gate can point at nothing. (c) check-io-seam.sh: make the scanner-failure branch unreachable (`[ \"$RC\" -eq 99 ] && { fail ...; }`) -- nothing exercises a crashing scanner. (a) is the one that matters, and it is a failure-path case the suite does not have at all: a fixture file made unreadable (chmod 000), asserting exit 1. (b) and (c) are cheap to fold into the cases that already read the output.

findings.title: The exemption's anchoring is unpinned -- unanchoring it leaves 9/9 green
findings.failure_scenario: SURVIVING MUTATION, RUN: `grep -v 'binstore-backends'` in place of `grep -v '^binstore-backends/'` in check-io-seam.sh. 9 of 9 green, because the adapter fixture's path starts with the string either way. The exemption is then a substring match anywhere in the path, so any future path containing `binstore-backends` -- a module renamed to `ingest-binstore-backends`, or a package directory named after it -- is silently exempted from non-negotiable 7. The case that exists (aFILESYSTEMReadIsACCEPTEDInTheAdapterAndREFUSEDOutsideIt) is the right shape and does load-bearing work on both halves; it just cannot see anchoring. One extra fixture path that CONTAINS but does not START WITH `binstore-backends`, asserting exit 1, pins it.

findings.title: The State cell says 'eight cases'; there are nine
findings.failure_scenario: Checkable against the diff, not a judgement: the M0.107 State cell says 'with eight cases in buildSrc/src/test/java/binjava/IoSeamGateTest.java', and IoSeamGateTest.java carries nine @Test methods (thisRepositoryPassesAndTheGateSaysHowManyFilesItRead, aBusinessLogicFileSOURCINGTheRealClockIsREFUSED, takingAClockAsASeamParameterIsACCEPTED, aFILESYSTEMReadIsACCEPTEDInTheAdapterAndREFUSEDOutsideIt, handlingAnInputStreamIsACCEPTEDWhileOPENINGOneIsNot, openingASOCKETFromBusinessLogicIsREFUSED, aBannedCallQUOTEDInAJavadocOrASTRINGIsNotAViolation, aChangeTouchingNOBusinessLogicFilePASSES, theGateSaysWhichSCOPEItRan). A count in prose beside a file that carries the real number is the class M5.34 spent four recurrences on: name them or drop the count. Reported because the parent asked for the State cell's claims to be checked; per review.md rule 11 it lands as a minor rather than buying a fix round. Every OTHER claim in that cell and in the class javadoc I checked out true: 103 tracked src/main binjava files, LocalFsBinStore the sole match (I ran the scanner over all 103 with the exemption removed -- 36 hits, all in that one file), the exemption argument, and both non-ban cases reddening under their widenings.

findings.title: 'LocalSequencer holds more business logic than any other file in the tree' is a superlative the tree does not support, restated in four places
findings.failure_scenario: Not a test-strength finding -- a claim in the class javadoc the parent put in scope. `wc -l` over the 103 tracked src/main binjava files puts LocalSequencer.java SECOND at 578 lines, behind ChainReplay.java at 604 (CommitLog 556, DefaultIngest 553, SubscriptionHub 552). 'More business logic than any other file' is either false on the only measure available or unmeasurable; the argument it supports does not need the superlative -- 'LocalSequencer implements Sequencer and is business logic' carries it completely. The same sentence appears in FOUR places in this diff (IoSeamGateTest javadoc, check-io-seam.sh header, code-structure.md rule 3, the backlog State cell), which is the restatement pattern this project has already been bitten by. Flagged, not asked to be fixed: review.md rule 11 says the next round's surface is the prose the fix adds, and four sites is four chances to introduce a new one.
